claims.text: The initial CoCrFeNiTi powder mixture is equiatomic, with 20 at.% of each element.
Mechanical alloying is performed for 20 hours in an argon atmosphere.
The proposed SPS treatment uses 950°C, 100°C/min heating, a 5-minute hold, and 60 MPa uniaxial pressure.
High-energy milling creates a high density of dislocations.
High-energy milling produces nanoscale mixing of the constituent elements.
Stored deformation energy from milling drives solid-state diffusion and grain-boundary migration during SPS.
The rapid SPS thermal cycle prevents the Ti-rich HCP phase from having enough time to nucleate and grow.
The SPS cycle provides enough diffusion to form a metastable FCC/BCC solid solution.
A uniaxial pressure of 60 MPa closes pores and suppresses porosity.
The applied pressure enhances atomic mobility through pressure-assisted diffusion.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between Ti and the other elements generates a high local strain rate and local stress fields during initial sintering.
The thermal-mismatch stress fields stabilize FCC against transformation to HCP.
The proposed process produces a density greater than 98% of theoretical density.
The proposed process produces grains approximately 50–100 nm in size.
The resulting alloy is dominated by FCC with a minor BCC phase.
The resulting alloy has a Vickers hardness of 450–550 HV.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi contains porosity.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has a coarse-grained single-phase FCC structure.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has a hardness of approximately 150–200 HV.
An SPS window of 850–1050°C provides sufficient diffusion while avoiding grain coarsening and HCP precipitation.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator says the cycle does not allow enough time for HCP nucleation, whereas the mechanism says the heating rate and dwell time 'exceed the critical nucleation rate for the HCP phase.' Taken literally, exceeding an HCP nucleation rate would promote rather than suppress nucleation, and heating rate and nucleation rate are also dimensionally different quantities.

The proposed control logic does not falsify grain-refinement strengthening: hardness equal to the Ti-free CoCrFeNi control is interpreted as negligible Ti solute strengthening, which is compatible with, rather than contrary to, hardness arising from grain refinement. The controls also do not hold grain size and phase fraction constant, so they cannot isolate solute strengthening.
